# Naren's Claude Toolkit

> Original Claude Code skills, mods and MCP servers by Naren. Install plugins through the plugin marketplace `NarenDawar/narens-claude-toolkit`.

## Skills

- [citation-verifier](https://github.com/NarenDawar/narens-claude-toolkit/blob/main/plugins/citation-verifier/README.md): Use when the user has a manuscript, bibliography, reference list or AI-written text with citations and wants to know whether the references are real and correctly cited, or whether the cited works actually say what the text claims (for example 'check my references', 'are these citations hallucinated?', 'does this paper really say that?').
- [comprehension-check](https://github.com/NarenDawar/narens-claude-toolkit/blob/main/plugins/comprehension-check/README.md): Use when the user asks to be quizzed on, or to check their understanding of, code Claude wrote this session (for example 'quiz me on that' or 'do I actually understand this change?').
- [deal-sparring-partner](https://github.com/NarenDawar/narens-claude-toolkit/blob/main/plugins/deal-sparring-partner/README.md): Use when the user is about to negotiate a purchase, rent, vendor, contract or service deal (a car, an apartment lease, a contractor quote, a subscription renewal) and wants to prepare, rehearse or practise it, or have the other side played back to them (for example 'help me negotiate this', 'play the landlord', 'let me practise before I call the dealer').
- [decision-journal](https://github.com/NarenDawar/narens-claude-toolkit/blob/main/plugins/decision-journal/README.md): Use when the user wants to log a prediction or estimate about a dev or project decision, grade past predictions, or see how calibrated they are (for example 'log a prediction', 'grade my predictions', 'how calibrated am I?').
- [human-writing](https://github.com/NarenDawar/narens-claude-toolkit/blob/main/plugins/human-writing/README.md): Use when the user wants words written or rewritten in a human, personal voice, including short casual messages: a Slack note, newsletter intro, cover letter, email, post, bio, speech or story, with or without a pasted voice sample. Also use when a draft sounds fake, robotic, generic, corporate or "ChatGPT-ish", even if they wrote it with an AI, and as a final pass on anything Claude drafted that the user will send or publish as themselves. Skip code, data, translation, proofreading-only requests, legal text, and anything whose exact wording must stay unchanged.
- [item-recommender](https://github.com/NarenDawar/narens-claude-toolkit/blob/main/plugins/item-recommender/README.md): Use when the user asks Claude to find, pick, compare or recommend a product to buy (for example 'find me the best toothbrush', 'which laptop should I get', 'best budget vacuum', 'X vs Y, which one?', 'what's worth buying for ...').
- [model-bakeoff](https://github.com/NarenDawar/narens-claude-toolkit/blob/main/plugins/model-bakeoff/README.md): Use when the user wants to pick the cheapest model that still works for a custom subagent, asks whether Haiku or Sonnet would do, or wants to re-check an agent's model after new models ship (for example 'which model should this agent use?', 'could this run on Haiku?', 'bake-off my reviewer agent').
- [news-source-reader](https://github.com/NarenDawar/narens-claude-toolkit/blob/main/plugins/news-source-reader/README.md): Use when the user shares a news article (link, saved page or pasted text) and asks how reliable or well sourced it is, who is behind the outlet, whether its claims hold up, or what it leaves out (for example 'is this article trustworthy?', 'where does this claim come from?', 'what's missing from this story?').
- [oss-issue-matcher](https://github.com/NarenDawar/narens-claude-toolkit/blob/main/plugins/oss-issue-matcher/README.md): Use when the user wants to find an open-source issue or project to contribute to, a good first issue, or help picking a repo whose maintainers will actually review and merge outside pull requests (for example 'find me a first open-source contribution', 'good first issues for Rust', 'is this repo worth contributing to').
- [pdf-table-fixer](https://github.com/NarenDawar/narens-claude-toolkit/blob/main/plugins/pdf-table-fixer/README.md): Use when the user has a tagged PDF whose tables fail accessibility checks or read badly in a screen reader (for example 'fix the table headers in this PDF', 'my PDF tables fail PDF/UA', 'repair the table tags').
- [platform-opportunity-scout](https://github.com/NarenDawar/narens-claude-toolkit/blob/main/plugins/platform-opportunity-scout/README.md): Use when the user names a platform or medium (Roblox, YouTube, Instagram, TikTok, Twitch, Etsy, Substack and the like) and wants business ideas built on or around it, or asks what to make, sell or build there (for example 'business ideas for Roblox', 'what could I build around YouTube creators', 'find me a niche on Instagram').
- [podcast-clip-scout](https://github.com/NarenDawar/narens-claude-toolkit/blob/main/plugins/podcast-clip-scout/README.md): Use when the user has a timestamped podcast or video transcript and wants the best short clips picked from it (for example 'find the best clips in this episode', 'which moments would work as shorts', 'pick reel candidates from this transcript').
- [rule-promoter](https://github.com/NarenDawar/narens-claude-toolkit/blob/main/plugins/rule-promoter/README.md): Use when the user wants rules in CLAUDE.md enforced with hooks, says Claude keeps ignoring a CLAUDE.md rule, or asks to turn CLAUDE.md rules into hooks (for example 'promote my CLAUDE.md rules to hooks' or 'make Claude stop editing migrations').
- [rules-referee](https://github.com/NarenDawar/narens-claude-toolkit/blob/main/plugins/rules-referee/README.md): Use when the user has a board game, card game or tabletop RPG rulebook (PDF or text) and wants a rules question or dispute settled, or asks what the rulebook actually says (for example 'does the rulebook let me do this?', 'we're arguing about a rule', 'settle this using the rulebook').
- [schedule-doctor](https://github.com/NarenDawar/narens-claude-toolkit/blob/main/plugins/schedule-doctor/README.md): Use when the user is about to schedule a Claude task, or asks why a scheduled task, /loop, cron job or routine did not run, ran late, or stopped partway (for example 'will this scheduled task actually run?', 'why didn't my 7am task fire?', 'check this before I schedule it').
- [straight-talk](https://github.com/NarenDawar/narens-claude-toolkit/blob/main/plugins/straight-talk/README.md): Use when giving an assessment, review or verdict on something the user made or decided, or when the user pushes back, shows hurt, or cites others' approval of work you rated lower.
- [subagent-tax-auditor](https://github.com/NarenDawar/narens-claude-toolkit/blob/main/plugins/subagent-tax-auditor/README.md): Use when the user asks why their Claude Code quota or usage limit runs out so fast, which subagents cost the most, or wants their subagents made cheaper (for example 'audit my subagents', 'which agent is eating my quota', 'make my agents cheaper').
- [training-load-watchdog](https://github.com/NarenDawar/narens-claude-toolkit/blob/main/plugins/training-load-watchdog/README.md): Use when a runner shares a Strava, Garmin or other activity export (CSV) and wants to know if their recent training looks risky, if they are ramping up too fast, or what the next weeks of running should be (for example 'check my training for injury risk', 'am I doing too much?', 'plan my next two weeks from my Strava export').
- [trip-expense-settler](https://github.com/NarenDawar/narens-claude-toolkit/blob/main/plugins/trip-expense-settler/README.md): Use when the user has a group's shared expenses (a chat log, notes, receipts, a messy list of who paid for what) from a trip, a house or an event and wants to know who owes whom and how to settle up with the fewest payments.

## Mods

- [clocks-band](https://github.com/NarenDawar/narens-claude-toolkit/blob/main/plugins/clocks-band/README.md): A band above the prompt showing every Bash command, MCP call and subagent that has run for a while, with elapsed time against its limit.
- [local-answer-router](https://github.com/NarenDawar/narens-claude-toolkit/blob/main/plugins/local-answer-router/README.md): Answers trivial questions (what branch, what changed, did the last test pass) from git and the last test run on your machine, with no model tokens.
- [subagent-meter](https://github.com/NarenDawar/narens-claude-toolkit/blob/main/plugins/subagent-meter/README.md): A live status line showing how much of your session's tokens go to subagents, and which agent type uses the most.

## MCP servers

- [anki-mcp](https://github.com/NarenDawar/narens-claude-toolkit/blob/main/servers/anki-mcp/README.md): Lets Claude quiz you on your due Anki cards, record your answers, and add flashcards without creating duplicates.
- [mcp-fixer](https://github.com/NarenDawar/narens-claude-toolkit/blob/main/servers/mcp-fixer/README.md): Scores an MCP server's tool definitions with deterministic lint rules, so you can see what makes agents pick the wrong tool or waste tokens.
